The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

# tree-sitter

Tree-sitter is a parser generator tool and an incremental parsing library. It can build a concrete syntax tree for a source file and efficiently update the syntax tree as the source file is edited.

## Features

Tree-sitter aims to be:

- **General** enough to parse any programming language
- **Fast** enough to parse on every keystroke in a text editor
- **Robust** enough to provide useful results even in the presence of syntax errors
- **Dependency-free** so that the runtime library can be embedded in any application

## What Tree-sitter Does

Tree-sitter can:

- Parse source code and build concrete syntax trees
- Incrementally update syntax trees as code is edited
- Perform syntax highlighting based on the parse tree
- Enable code navigation and analysis features
- Support querying the syntax tree with a pattern matching language

## Command Line Interface

The Tree-sitter CLI provides commands for:

- **parse** - Parse source files using Tree-sitter parsers
- **query** - Query syntax trees using Tree-sitter query language
- **highlight** - Apply syntax highlighting to source files
- **tags** - Generate code navigation tags

## Language Support

Tree-sitter supports parsing any programming language through language-specific parser modules. Parsers are available for many popular languages including JavaScript, Python, Rust, Go, C, C++, TypeScript, Java, Ruby, PHP, and many others.

Each parser is a separate module that can be used independently or together with the Tree-sitter runtime.

## Usage

Tree-sitter is designed to be embedded in text editors, IDEs, and other code analysis tools. The library provides APIs for:

- Parsing source code and obtaining syntax trees
- Traversing and inspecting nodes in the syntax tree
- Executing queries to find specific patterns in the code
- Applying incremental edits and re-parsing efficiently
- Extracting information for syntax highlighting and code navigation

Tree-sitter is used by several popular text editors and tools for syntax highlighting, code folding, and structural navigation.
</output>

_tree-sitter() {
    local i cur prev opts cmd
    COMPREPLY=()
    if [[ "${BASH_VERSINFO[0]}" -ge 4 ]]; then
        cur="$2"
    else
        cur="${COMP_WORDS[COMP_CWORD]}"
    fi
    prev="$3"
    cmd=""
    opts=""

    for i in "${COMP_WORDS[@]:0:COMP_CWORD}"
    do
        case "${cmd},${i}" in
            ",$1")
                cmd="tree__sitter"
                ;;
            tree__sitter,build)
                cmd="tree__sitter__build"
                ;;
            tree__sitter,complete)
                cmd="tree__sitter__complete"
                ;;
            tree__sitter,dump-languages)
                cmd="tree__sitter__dump__languages"
                ;;
            tree__sitter,fuzz)
                cmd="tree__sitter__fuzz"
                ;;
            tree__sitter,generate)
                cmd="tree__sitter__generate"
                ;;
            tree__sitter,highlight)
                cmd="tree__sitter__highlight"
                ;;
            tree__sitter,init)
                cmd="tree__sitter__init"
                ;;
            tree__sitter,init-config)
                cmd="tree__sitter__init__config"
                ;;
            tree__sitter,parse)
                cmd="tree__sitter__parse"
                ;;
            tree__sitter,playground)
                cmd="tree__sitter__playground"
                ;;
            tree__sitter,query)
                cmd="tree__sitter__query"
                ;;
            tree__sitter,tags)
                cmd="tree__sitter__tags"
                ;;
            tree__sitter,test)
                cmd="tree__sitter__test"
                ;;
            tree__sitter,version)
                cmd="tree__sitter__version"
                ;;
            *)
                ;;
        esac
    done

    case "${cmd}" in
        tree__sitter)
            opts="-h -V --help --version init-config init generate build parse test version fuzz query highlight tags playground dump-languages complete"
            if [[ ${cur} == -* || ${COMP_CWORD} -eq 1 ]] ; then
                COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "${opts}" -- "${cur}") )
                return 0
            fi
            case "${prev}" in
                *)
                    COMPREPLY=()
                    ;;
            esac
            COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "${opts}" -- "${cur}") )
            return 0
            ;;
        tree__sitter__build)
            opts="-w -o -0 -v -h --wasm --output --reuse-allocator --debug --verbose --help [PATH]"
            if [[ ${cur} == -* || ${COMP_CWORD} -eq 2 ]] ; then
                COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "${opts}" -- "${cur}") )
                return 0
            fi
            case "${prev}" in
                --output)
                    COMPREPLY=($(compgen -f "${cur}"))
                    return 0
                    ;;
                -o)
                    COMPREPLY=($(compgen -f "${cur}"))
                    return 0
                    ;;
                *)
                    COMPREPLY=()
                    ;;
            esac
            COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "${opts}" -- "${cur}") )
</output>

add_custom_command(OUTPUT "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/parser.c"

</output>

#include <napi.h>

typedef struct TSLanguage TSLanguage;

extern "C" TSLanguage *tree_sitter_myfresh();

// "tree-sitter", "language" hashed with BLAKE2
const napi_type_tag LANGUAGE_TYPE_TAG = {
    0x8AF2E5212AD58ABF, 0xD5006CAD83ABBA16
};

Napi::Object Init(Napi::Env env, Napi::Object exports) {
    auto language = Napi::External<TSLanguage>::New(env, tree_sitter_myfresh());
    language.TypeTag(&LANGUAGE_TYPE_TAG);
    exports["language"] = language;
    return exports;
}

NODE_API_MODULE(tree_sitter_myfresh_binding, Init)
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

const root = fileURLToPath(new URL("../..", import.meta.url));

const binding = typeof process.versions.bun === "string"
  // Support `bun build --compile` by being statically analyzable enough to find the .node file at build-time
  ? await import(`${root}/prebuilds/${process.platform}-${process.arch}/tree-sitter-myfresh.node`)
  : (await import("node-gyp-build")).default(root);

try {
  const nodeTypes = await import(`${root}/src/node-types.json`, { with: { type: "json" } });
  binding.nodeTypeInfo = nodeTypes.default;
} catch { }

const queries = [
  ["HIGHLIGHTS_QUERY", `${root}/queries/highlights.scm`],
  ["INJECTIONS_QUERY", `${root}/queries/injections.scm`],
  ["LOCALS_QUERY", `${root}/queries/locals.scm`],
  ["TAGS_QUERY", `${root}/queries/tags.scm`],
];

for (const [prop, path] of queries) {
  Object.defineProperty(binding, prop, {
    configurable: true,
    enumerable: true,
    get() {
      delete binding[prop];
      try {
        binding[prop] = readFileSync(path, "utf8");
      } catch { }
      return binding[prop];
    }
  });
}

export default binding;
type BaseNode = {
  type: string;
  named: boolean;
};

type ChildNode = {
  multiple: boolean;
  required: boolean;
  types: BaseNode[];
};

import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

const root = fileURLToPath(new URL("../..", import.meta.url));

const binding = typeof process.versions.bun === "string"
  // Support `bun build --compile` by being statically analyzable enough to find the .node file at build-time
  ? await import(`${root}/prebuilds/${process.platform}-${process.arch}/tree-sitter-myfresh.node`)
  : (await import("node-gyp-build")).default(root);

try {
  const nodeTypes = await import(`${root}/src/node-types.json`, { with: { type: "json" } });

SONAME_MINOR = $(word 1,$(subst ., ,$(VERSION)))

//! This crate provides Myfresh language support for the [tree-sitter] parsing library.
//!
//! Typically, you will use the [`LANGUAGE`] constant to add this language to a
//! tree-sitter [`Parser`], and then use the parser to parse some code:
//!
//! ```
//! let code = r#"
//! "#;
//! let mut parser = tree_sitter::Parser::new();
//! let language = tree_sitter_myfresh::LANGUAGE;
//! parser
//!     .set_language(&language.into())
//!     .expect("Error loading Myfresh parser");
//! let tree = parser.parse(code, None).unwrap();
//! assert!(!tree.root_node().has_error());
//! ```
//!
//! [`Parser`]: https://docs.rs/tree-sitter/0.27.0/tree_sitter/struct.Parser.html
//! [tree-sitter]: https://tree-sitter.github.io/

use tree_sitter_language::LanguageFn;

unsafe extern "C" {
    fn tree_sitter_myfresh() -> *const ();
}

/// The tree-sitter [`LanguageFn`] for this grammar.
pub const LANGUAGE: LanguageFn = unsafe { LanguageFn::from_raw(tree_sitter_myfresh) };

/// The content of the [`node-types.json`] file for this grammar.
fn main() {
    let src_dir = std::path::Path::new("src");

    let mut c_config = cc::Build::new();
    c_config.std("c11").include(src_dir);

    #[cfg(target_env = "msvc")]
    c_config.flag("-utf-8");

    if std::env::var("TARGET").unwrap() == "wasm32-unknown-unknown" {
        let Ok(wasm_headers) = std::env::var("DEP_TREE_SITTER_LANGUAGE_WASM_HEADERS") else {
            panic!("Environment variable DEP_TREE_SITTER_LANGUAGE_WASM_HEADERS must be set by the language crate");
        };
        let Ok(wasm_src) =
            std::env::var("DEP_TREE_SITTER_LANGUAGE_WASM_SRC").map(std::path::PathBuf::from)
        else {
            panic!("Environment variable DEP_TREE_SITTER_LANGUAGE_WASM_SRC must be set by the language crate");
        };

        c_config.include(&wasm_headers);
        c_config.files([
            wasm_src.join("stdio.c"),
            wasm_src.join("stdlib.c"),
            wasm_src.join("string.c"),
        ]);
    }

    let parser_path = src_dir.join("parser.c");
    c_config.file(&parser_path);
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={}", parser_path.to_str().unwrap());

    let scanner_path = src_dir.join("scanner.c");
    if scanner_path.exists() {
        c_config.file(&scanner_path);
        println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed={}", scanner_path.to_str().unwrap());
    }

    c_config.compile("tree-sitter-myfresh");

    println!("cargo:rustc-check-cfg=cfg(with_highlights_query)");
    if !"queries/highlights.scm".is_empty() && std::path::Path::new("queries/highlights.scm").exists() {
        println!("cargo:rustc-cfg=with_highlights_query");
    }
    println!("cargo:rustc-check-cfg=cfg(with_injections_query)");
    if !"queries/injections.scm".is_empty() && std::path::Path::new("queries/injections.scm").exists() {
        println!("cargo:rustc-cfg=with_injections_query");
    }
    println!("cargo:rustc-check-cfg=cfg(with_locals_query)");
    if !"queries/locals.scm".is_empty() && std::path::Path::new("queries/locals.scm").exists() {
        println!("cargo:rustc-cfg=with_locals_query");
    }
    println!("cargo:rustc-check-cfg=cfg(with_tags_query)");
    if !"queries/tags.scm".is_empty() && std::path::Path::new("queries/tags.scm").exists() {
        println!("cargo:rustc-cfg=with_tags_query");
    }
}
</output>
